paper_metadata.title: Experimental Demonstration of Fermionic QAOA with One-Dimensional Cyclic Driver Hamiltonian

summary: The paper demonstrates fermionic QAOA for an 8-asset portfolio optimization problem on 16 qubits, using a new cyclic driver Hamiltonian that reduces gate counts from O(N^2D) to O(ND). In noiseless simulation, cyc-FQAOA and ladder-FQAOA achieve similar low energies (0.13 ± 0.13 vs 0.12 ± 0.13), while on IonQ Aria the cyclic version improves the post-selected low-energy peak and yields a lower reported energy expectation (0.23 ± 0.16) than the ladder baseline (0.34 ± 0.17).

experiments.description: Noiseless simulation of fermionic QAOA (FQAOA) with the proposed cyclic driver Hamiltonian for the portfolio optimization problem, compared against ladder-lattice FQAOA and XY-QAOA baseline.

algorithm.variant: Fermionic QAOA with one-dimensional cyclic driver Hamiltonian
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Time-discretized QAA schedule used as initial angles: gamma_j^(0) = (2j-1)/(2p) * Δt, beta_j^(0) = (1-(2j-1)/(2p)) * Δt

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Unary encoding with one fermionic occupation qubit per binary variable x_{l,d}; total particle number constraint enforced as fixed Hamming weight M = ND/2 - K
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize portfolio cost E(x) = λ/K^2 * sum_{l,l'} σ_{l,l'} sum_{d,d'} (n_{l,d}-1/2)(n_{l',d'}-1/2) + (1-λ)/K * sum_l μ_l sum_d (n_{l,d}-1/2)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard constraint via fermion-number-conserving driver Hamiltonian; no penalty term. Post-selection used only in QPU experiment, not in this noiseless simulation.

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization instance from prior work, using 8 assets and 2 discretization levels per asset.

dataset_specification.description: Covariance matrix σ_{l,l'} from Ref. [2] Fig. 2 and expected returns μ_l from Ref. [2] Table IV; λ = 0.9, N = 8, D = 2, K = 4

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noiseless simulation; probability distributions and energy expectation values reported for p = 1 and p = 4; BFGS optimization from QAA-initialized angles

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Parameters initialized from discretized QAA schedule; BFGS used for variational optimization

speedup_claims.conditions: No asymptotic or computational speedup claim; paper focuses on noise reduction and gate-count reduction.
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not claim quantum advantage; it reports comparable noiseless performance and improved robustness to noise.

speedup_claims.conditions: QPU experiment at p=1, comparing probability of obtaining low-cost solutions in the lowest-energy region after debiasing and post-selection.
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an empirical improvement in low-cost-solution probability, not a runtime speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require substantially larger problem sizes and a demonstrated asymptotic speedup; current result is a shallow p=1 simulation on 16 qubits.
limiting_factors: No classical solver runtime benchmark against the quantum method
Only 16 qubits and p = 1 / p = 4 shallow-depth demonstrations
Performance gain is only relative to an alternative quantum baseline

experiments.description: Real-hardware trapped-ion QPU experiment of FQAOA with the proposed cyclic driver Hamiltonian for the portfolio optimization problem, using debiasing and post-selection.

algorithm.variant: Fermionic QAOA with one-dimensional cyclic driver Hamiltonian on trapped-ion QPU
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Variational parameters taken from noiseless simulation; initial schedule based on discretized QAA

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Unary encoding with 16 fermionic occupation qubits; constraint on total fermion number M = 4 enforced by number-conserving mixer and post-selection on measured bitstrings
problem_formulation.objective_function: Same portfolio optimization Hamiltonian as in exp_1
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard constraint via fermion-number-conserving driver Hamiltonian; debiasing applied; post-selection to samples satisfying M = 4

problem_instance.description: Same 8-asset portfolio optimization instance as in the noiseless simulation.

dataset_specification.description: Covariance matrix σ_{l,l'} from Ref. [2] Fig. 2 and expected returns μ_l from Ref. [2] Table IV; λ = 0.9, N = 8, D = 2, K = 4

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10,000 measurements with debiasing; post-selection on M = 4; compared against random sampling under the same constraint and against ladder-lattice FQAOA

noise_model.mitigation_details: Debiasing applied to 10,000 measurements; sharpening not applied; post-selection retained only samples with total fermion number M = 4

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Noiseless simulation used to determine variational parameters before QPU execution
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Debiasing and post-selection; energy distribution and expectation value computed from accepted samples

speedup_claims.conditions: QPU experiment at p=1 with debiasing and post-selection; comparing low-cost-solution probability in the lowest-energy region.
speedup_claims.caveats: Not a computational speedup; improvement is attributed to reduced gate count and reduced noise sensitivity.

speedup_claims.conditions: No asymptotic speedup or quantum advantage claim is made.
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper only reports better empirical performance than ladder-lattice FQAOA and random constrained sampling.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would need larger instances, lower noise, and a classical baseline runtime/quality comparison; current experiment is 16-qubit trapped-ion QPU with post-selection.
limiting_factors: Heavy reliance on debiasing and post-selection
Improvement is only relative to ladder-FQAOA, not classical methods

notes: num_qubits inferred as 16 from N = 8 and D = 2 with unary encoding (ND qubits).
